steps: 1. Write the contract before code. Add docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity.md (task breakdown, the assumptions below, and what each step makes harder later). Add a 'Checksum-Compatible Resume Projection Integrity' section to specs/state.md covering items 1-8: audit order, explicit-identity and omission rules, the four repeat_until progress forms, call-frame retry lineage, the checksum and projection envelopes, sticky non-routable failure plus supplemental finalization, the diagnostic schema v1 with the twelve reasons, and privacy. Add matching numbered entries to specs/acceptance/index.md next to entries 197/199. State schema stays 2.1. Files: docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity.md, specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md.

2. Typed Workflow Lisp provenance (item 8). Add an optional frontend_kind parameter to the WorkflowProvenance construction in elaborate_surface_workflow (orchestrator/workflow/elaboration.py ~line 206). Pass frontend_kind="workflow_lisp" from _validate_one_lowered_workflow (orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/core.py ~line 2433); every lowered, validated and imported Workflow Lisp bundle goes through that path. First confirm that build_loaded_workflow_bundle (orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py) takes provenance from the surface. In build_frontend_bundle (orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py ~line 385), replace the literal frontend_kind="workflow_lisp" with selected_bundle.provenance.frontend_kind. Check that classic-YAML bundles in imported_workflow_bundles are linked as the same object with no copy (orchestrator/workflow_lisp/workflows.py ~lines 818 and 1049, lowering/core.py ~line 967). Change CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target (orchestrator/workflow/calls.py:41) to `provenance.frontend_kind == "workflow_lisp"` and drop the .orc suffix test. Tests: new tests/test_workflow_lisp_bundle_provenance.py, which compiles a small .orc with an imported .orc and an imported YAML workflow through compile_stage3_entrypoint and build_frontend_bundle and checks the kinds and the YAML object identity. Run pytest on that file and on tests/test_workflow_lisp_build_artifacts.py.

3. Classic-YAML duplicate import aliases (item 5). Add orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py (about 120 lines). It exposes import_alias_errors(text) -> list[str], which runs yaml.compose with PreservingLoader and walks the top-level MappingNode. It collects every `imports` key, including those reached through top-level `<<` merge sources (an alias node, a mapping, or a sequence of them). For each it expands `<<` inside imports and gathers each alias key node with its start_mark rendered as `line L, column C` (1-based). It reports `imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias` once per repeated alias, listing every position. If there are several imports sections and all aliases are unique, it reports `imports: duplicate top-level mapping` once, with the position of each imports key. A repeated alias suppresses the section error. In WorkflowLoader._load_workflow (orchestrator/loader.py ~line 175), read the file text once, run the check and yaml.load on that text, and on errors call _add_error for each and return {} before _load_imports, elaborate_surface_workflow and build_loaded_workflow_bundle. load_bundle then raises WorkflowValidationError. Tests: new tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py covers duplicate keys, `<<` inside imports, repeated sections, merged-plus-explicit sections, top-level merge sources that each carry imports, distinct-alias repeated sections, and the single merged section that loads. Each test substitutes orchestrator.loader.build_loaded_workflow_bundle with a sentinel to prove it is never reached on failure.

4. Projection data the auditor needs. Add `import_alias: Optional[str] = None` to CallBoundaryProjection and `max_iterations: Optional[int] = None` to IterationStepKeyProjection (orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py). Populate them in orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py: register_call_boundary takes the call step's authored `call` alias, and the repeat_until registration takes the declared max_iterations. Check the other consumers of call_boundaries (orchestrator/workflow/runtime_plan.py:400,584) still work. Tests: extend tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py to show that a loaded YAML call boundary carries its alias and that keyword construction works.

5. Resume slot enumeration and loop bookkeeping validation (items 2-3). Add orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py with frozen dataclasses ResumeProjectionSlot (node_id, step_id, presentation_key, region, iteration_index), ResumeProjectionSlotIndex (candidates_by_step_id, call_boundaries_by_step_id, unclaimed_explicit_rows) and the resolution results. Its pure enumerate function reads only the projection and the state: top-level body and finalization entries; loop-local runtime ids `<loop>#<i>.<suffix>`, but only for iterations the validated for_each or repeat_until bookkeeping admits; call boundaries keyed by runtime step id (call_boundary_runtime_step_id); and unclaimed explicit rows as snapshotted (name, step_id) pairs. It validates for_each indices (unique non-bool non-negative ints in range, current_index in range and not completed) and the four repeat_until forms, raising ResumeProjectionValidationError(reason, message) with exactly the listed messages; successful exhaustion checks for a completed loop row and failed exhaustion for error.type repeat_until_iterations_exhausted. It never mutates or backfills the state. In state_projection.py, define ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) (with .reason and .message, str() equal to the message) and add three thin methods that delegate to resume_slots: enumerate_resume_slots(state), resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None), which returns 0 candidates for unhashable or malformed ids, and resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id). This keeps state_projection.py under 500 lines. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_slots.py, one behaviour per test, covering each message string, loop-local and finalization slots, unhashable ids, and non-mutation via a deepcopy comparison.

6. Call-frame retry lineage (item 4). Add orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_lineage.py with RetryFrameMember(frame_id, ordinal), CallFrameMember(frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage(base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Rules: completed frames are unlimited history. For a non-Workflow-Lisp boundary there is at most one non-completed frame, and it becomes running_member. For Workflow Lisp, parse `B` or `B::retry::<n>` (n a positive int with no leading junk); a nested marker, a bad ordinal or an unknown status gives unsupported_shape; mixed bases, a duplicate ordinal or more than one running member gives ambiguous_resumable_call_frame; a missing ordinal (a gap among non-completed members, completed counted as present) gives unsupported_shape; a call_step_id that is not the boundary gives missing_call_boundary; differing aliases give persisted_import_alias_mismatch. The result never depends on mapping order, and the next id is the lowest positive ordinal unused across all members. Remove the mapping-order helpers _retry_frame_id, _retry_family_base and _is_failed_retry_family_frame from calls.py once step 9 replaces their callers (validate_write_root_bindings uses the lineage instead). Tests: new tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py.

7. The auditor (items 1, 2, 4, 7). Add orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (target under 400 lines; it imports nothing from workflow_lisp.migration_parity or procedure_identity_retirement, and no name or string in it contains receipt or audit/cache wording). It defines ResumeScopePath (frozen; call_frame_ids snapshotted to a tuple; root(), child(), projection_scope, as_context()), ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) with .error, and a single _fail(reason, *, field, offending_value, candidate_count, call_boundary_step_id) builder that always emits all seven context keys. It nulls offending_value for containers and never echoes contents. It re-exports index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id, CallFrameRetryLineage, RetryFrameMember and CallFrameRetryLineageError from call_frame_lineage. audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path) runs in a fixed order so the diagnostic is stable. (a) Container shapes: `steps` and `call_frames` must be mappings, each frame a mapping. (b) Enumerate slots, mapping ResumeProjectionValidationError to unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress with the field taken from the message. (c) Step rows in sorted name order: an absent step_id is skipped; otherwise check type, then unknown, presentation mismatch, or unclaimed. (d) current_step: a missing step_id gives missing_required_identity, else resolve (out_of_scope or presentation mismatch). (e) Frames in sorted id order: a missing call_step_id is missing_required_identity; a non-local id is out_of_scope_step_id; a local non-boundary is missing_call_boundary; more than one owner is ambiguous_call_boundary; an alias that differs from boundary.import_alias is persisted_import_alias_mismatch; an alias absent from bundle.imports is missing_imported_bundle. (f) Group frames per boundary and run index_retry_lineage with frontend_kind taken from the imported bundle's provenance, translating lineage reasons. The auditor reads only its arguments: no loads, no checksum, no files, no mutation. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py builds bundles with WorkflowLoader in tmp_path and has one test per reason, plus scope path, expected_owner, the privacy cases (a malformed list id gives a null offending value; no bound_inputs or context in the diagnostic) and a deepcopy non-mutation check. Add one small source-scan test for the forbidden imports and words.

8. StateManager envelopes (item 6). In orchestrator/state.py add a private _record_terminal_error(error) that, under the lock, sets status='failed' and error, then calls _write_state() (updated_at bumps as today). It leaves current_step, the run tree and unknown fields alone and does not call fail_run. Add record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason), which validates the reason against the four literals and builds the fixed message and context, and record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error). Tests: extend tests/test_state_manager.py to compare state.json before and after, showing only status, error and updated_at change.

9. Root guard in the CLI (items 1 and 6). In orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, add the module-level `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, ResumeScopePath, audit_scope` and always call it as the bare name audit_scope. Move the _merge_observability_overrides persist block (currently ~lines 390-406, before workflow load) to after the checksum precheck. On the non-force-restart path, right after validate_checksum passes, call audit_scope(workflow_bundle, state.to_dict(), ResumeScopePath.root(state.workflow_file)). On failure call record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error), print the message (with the reason) to stderr and return 1, before observability persist, open_executor_session, write_process_metadata, WorkflowExecutor construction and the prologue. Keep the existing checksum precheck as it is (exit 1, nothing written). In the finally block, close the executor session as failed when the executor returned a projection or checksum error. If close fails, log it and keep the persisted diagnostic. Tests: extend tests/test_resume_command.py. Substitute orchestrator.cli.commands.resume.audit_scope, open_executor_session and WorkflowExecutor with recorders to prove ordering, and check exit 1, stderr, and the three-field state delta.

10. Root guard in the executor (items 1 and 6). Add orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py with root_checksum_failure(state_manager, state) -> Optional[dict]. It recomputes through state_manager.calculate_checksum(Path(workflow_file)) and returns the reason as workflow_modified, missing_recorded_checksum, missing_workflow_path or workflow_unavailable (FileNotFoundError). In orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, add a module-level import of audit_scope (called by the bare name) and a short _resume_root_guard(state) used in execute() before _execute_prologue, only when resume is true and the state manager is not a CallFrameStateManager. On a checksum failure it calls record_workflow_checksum_mismatch and returns the reloaded state without auditing. Otherwise it calls audit_scope(self.loaded_bundle, state, ResumeScopePath.root(...)), and on failure calls record_resume_projection_integrity_failure and returns the reloaded state, with no prologue. Tests: in tests/test_resume_command.py or new tests/test_executor_resume_root_guard.py, (a) mutate the workflow between the CLI audit and executor construction (a checksum race) and check the envelope; (b) substitute executor.audit_scope so the second audit fails after the CLI audit passed, and check the three-field delta, that session and process metadata are kept, and that the session closes as failed; (c) check that a child call-frame executor never calls the root guard.

11. Reached-call validation and lineage selection (items 1 and 4). In orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, add the module-level audit_scope import and call it by the bare name. Replace the mapping-order branch of frame_id_with_overrides with deterministic selection. Order in execute_call: keep alias, bound-input, finalize, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input validation where they are. Before them, under resume_mode, call projection.resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, step_id) once (positional) on the parent slot index; zero or several owners gives a projection error, and the boundary's import_alias picks the callee through workflow_import_bundle, so step['call'] and the persisted alias are only checked. Check for a completed-frame collision on the visit frame id (the frame the call would occupy) before any grouping; it returns resume_state_invalid_result(detail="completed_call_frame_id_collision") with no child manager or executor and the frames unchanged. Then run index_retry_lineage over frames for this boundary. With a running member, its validate_resume_checksum and validate_resume_bound_inputs run first and win; then each failed predecessor in ordinal order gets validate_resume_checksum plus audit_scope(callee, pred['state'], scope.child(pred_id)); then audit_scope on the running member's state; then the child is built. With no running member, predecessors are validated and audited, then the frame is next_unused_retry_frame_id (Workflow Lisp) or the visit id. Derive the scope path by walking the _CallFrameStateManager.parent_manager chain, with a small helper in orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py. A ResumeProjectionIntegrityError or lineage error becomes {status: failed, exit_code: 2, error: exc.error}. When child_state fails with error.type resume_projection_integrity_error, return that error unchanged and not call_failed. Tests: extend tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py with a stale caller, an alias change, two resumable frames, the retry lineage cases (failed predecessors audited, a gap, mixed bases), the collision context exact dict, precedence of call_resume_checksum_mismatch, and the callee frame untouched (substituting orchestrator.workflow.calls.audit_scope to observe ordering).

12. Sticky non-routable failure and promotion (item 6). In WorkflowExecutor._handle_control_flow (orchestrator/workflow/executor.py ~line 3995), return '_stop' for error_type resume_projection_integrity_error next to cycle_guard_exceeded, before goto, on_error=continue and strict_flow. Make sure the run-error promotion path (executor.py ~line 2043 and _execute_epilogue) copies that step error unchanged to the root error and that later steps cannot clear or replace it. In orchestrator/workflow/loops.py (the for_each nested-failure break ~line 1067, the repeat_until condition and exhaustion path ~lines 1266-1420), stop at once on that error type: the loop step fails with the same error, with no next iteration, no condition evaluation and no exhaustion result. In orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, record_step_result and record_settled_result keep finalization running for configured cleanup, but when the run already carries a projection diagnostic, a cleanup failure is recorded as status failed and failure={step, step_id, error: the projection error or null}, and state['error'] is never replaced. A projection error raised only inside finalization becomes the run error and failure.error. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py drives YAML workflows with success, failure and always gotos, on_error=continue, for_each and repeat_until, and a finally block through the resume command or executor, with a stale nested call identity to trigger the error.

13. Forensic current_step in observability (item 6). In orchestrator/observability/report.py, add _is_forensic_current_step(state), true when status is failed and error.type is resume_projection_integrity_error or workflow_checksum_mismatch. In build_status_snapshot (~lines 299-332), treat that step as not current: status and summary pending, current_visit_count null, counted as pending. render_status_markdown then never shows 'in progress'. Make the heartbeat helper (~line 234) ignore it. Check orchestrator/dashboard/cursor.py and orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py; the classifier already returns FAILED before any heartbeat check, so change the cursor only if it reports the node as live. Tests: extend tests/test_observability_report.py.

14. Verification and wrap-up. Run pytest --collect-only on every new or renamed test module. Run the narrow selectors from steps 2-13, then the neighbouring suites: tests/test_resume_command.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py, tests/test_state_manager.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py, tests/test_observability_report.py, tests/test_at68_resume_force_restart.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py and the workflow_lisp build tests. For the end-to-end smoke check, run `python -m orchestrator run` then `resume` on workflows/examples/for_each_demo.yaml and finally_demo.yaml. Hand-edit one state.json step_id to see the exit-1 projection diagnostic and the three-field delta. Check that new modules stay under 500 lines. Commit after each green step (no --no-verify). Open assumptions to confirm with the user: (a) the CLI audit also runs for status 'completed' runs, because it precedes the early 'already completed' return under the literal ordering; (b) finalization.failure.error is null for ordinary cleanup failures only when the run carries a projection diagnostic, and existing non-projection behaviour is unchanged.

findings: [P0] Steps 5/7/8 cannot guarantee the promised stable error or three-field state delta through StateManager.load(). RunState.from_dict constructs ForEachState(**state_dict), so malformed for_each entries can raise before audit_scope; RunState.to_dict also discards unknown root fields, so _record_terminal_error -> _write_state silently deletes them. Audit the raw persisted state before typed conversion, or preserve its raw fields in the failure writer, and test malformed for_each plus unknown-field retention (orchestrator/state.py:160,335).

[P0] Step 11 places reached-call auditing inside execute_call, after the parent executor has called start_step and persisted current_step (and loop execution can persist progress before nested calls). A stale callee identity therefore fails only after mutation, violating the stated before-any-mutation/effect boundary. Add a pre-persistence reached-call guard at the top-level and loop dispatch points, or explicitly narrow and justify the mutation contract (orchestrator/workflow/executor.py:3070-3090; orchestrator/workflow/loops.py:933-1110).

[P0] Steps 9/10 contradict the three-field failure envelope for the executor's second audit. The CLI opens and writes an executor session before execute(); its finally block closes and writes that session after the guard returns a projection/checksum error. runtime_observability therefore changes in addition to status, error, and updated_at, and process metadata may be written. Rework where the second guard runs or state explicitly that this envelope excludes session/process metadata; the proposed test asserting both a three-field delta and a closed session cannot pass (orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py:522-606).

[P1] Step 6 groups all frames by call boundary and treats mixed retry bases as ambiguous, while allowing unlimited completed history. Normal repeated visits to one call produce distinct '<step_id>::visit::<n>' bases under the same call_step_id, so a valid resumed goto/revisited call would be rejected. Partition lineage by visit base, validate all completed families independently, and select only the current visit family for retry allocation (orchestrator/workflow/calls.py:132-168).

[P1] Step 11 explicitly maps a completed-frame collision to resume_state_invalid_result instead of resume_projection_integrity_error. This is a newly detected persisted call-frame identity conflict, so it violates the intended single stable, non-downgradable integrity diagnostic. Include it in the projection error reason set and test its exact root promotion (orchestrator/workflow/calls.py:556,784).

[P1] Step 7's privacy rule only nulls container-valued offending_value. Arbitrarily long or sensitive scalar step IDs, aliases, frame IDs, and scope-path strings can still be copied into the error context or message; sorting malformed mixed-type mapping keys may also throw before _fail. Define bounded/redacted rendering and deterministic safe ordering for untrusted keys, then test oversized strings and non-string keys.

[P2] Step 9 audits only after _load_resume_workflow_bundle. For .orc resumes that function invokes build_frontend_bundle, which creates .orchestrate/build directories and writes artifacts before the checksum and projection checks. If 'before any mutation or effect' covers filesystem build artifacts, the plan needs a read-only compile/audit path or a precise exception for those artifacts (orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py:190-240; orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py:383-390).

[P2] The plan adds a normative contract but omits the current documentation route: docs/capability_status_matrix.md still says the 2026-07-13 design-and-planning plan is the live prerequisite and that runtime hardening is not implemented; docs/design/README.md likewise routes to that plan. Update those maintained routes when this work lands, or readers will be sent to stale implementation status (docs/capability_status_matrix.md:34; docs/design/README.md:79).

Add a 'Checksum-Compatible Resume Projection Integrity' section to specs/state.md covering items 1-8: audit order, explicit-identity and omission rules, the four repeat_until progress forms, call-frame retry lineage partitioned by visit base, the checksum and projection envelopes, sticky non-routable failure plus supplemental finalization, diagnostic schema v1 with the twelve reasons, and privacy. Add matching numbered entries to specs/acceptance/index.md next to entries 197/199. State schema stays 2.1. The spec section must state these boundaries, which address review findings. (i) Mutation boundary per scope. The root audits (CLI and executor) run before any write to the run directory or any effect, apart from the .orc build artifacts in (iv). A reached call is different: item 1 orders callee validation after the parent's ordinary call visit/start publication, so the parent's ordinary pre-dispatch bookkeeping may already be persisted when a reached-call audit fails. That bookkeeping is current_step, step_visits, the provider-session visit preparation, and for a call inside a loop the loop's iteration progress written before the nested call. Every parent-scope identity (the frame's call_step_id, alias, boundary ownership and lineage shape) is already checked by the pre-mutation root audit, so only a checksum-compatible race or a callee-internal identity can fail at that point. The reached-call guarantee is therefore: no callee frame or state is created or changed, no callee effect runs, no further parent effect runs, and the parent's bookkeeping is overwritten by the ordinary failed call-step snapshot of item 6. (ii) Envelope baseline. The three-field delta is measured across the failure write itself. Session and process metadata opened earlier by the CLI are outside the envelope, as item 6 says, and so is the CLI's later session-close write, which only adds the closed-session record to runtime_observability. (iii) The completed-frame collision keeps the contract_violation shape that item 4 mandates (the twelve-reason set is closed), but it is sticky and is promoted unchanged, like a projection error (see step 12). Record this as a surfaced contradiction between item 4 and the single-diagnostic goal. (iv) .orc build artifacts. For .orc resumes, _load_resume_workflow_bundle -> build_frontend_bundle writes derived artifacts under the workspace build directory (.orchestrate/build) before the checksum and audit. Those artifacts are a rebuildable compile output, not run state, memo or a workflow effect, so they are the one stated exception. A read-only compile route would be an unrelated resume refactor that the constraints exclude. (v) Bounded scalar rendering (step 7). Mapping keys that are not strings, or that exceed the safe-key bound of step 7, are rejected as unsupported_shape before any sort or any field-path rendering. In state_projection.py, define ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) (.reason and .message, str() equal to the message) and add three thin methods that delegate to resume_slots: enumerate_resume_slots(state); resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None), which returns 0 candidates for unhashable or malformed ids; and resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id). This keeps state_projection.py under 500 lines. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_slots.py, one behaviour per test: each message string, loop-local and finalization slots, unhashable ids, a non-string mapping key, and non-mutation via a deepcopy comparison.

6. Call-frame retry lineage, partitioned by visit base (item 4). Add orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_lineage.py with RetryFrameMember(frame_id, ordinal), CallFrameMember(frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage(base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Revisiting a call (goto, or a loop iteration of the parent) legitimately produces distinct bases `<prefix><step_id>::visit::<n>` under one call_step_id. So every frame id is parsed into (visit base, ordinal), where the base is the id with at most one trailing `::retry::<n>` removed, and frames are partitioned into families by base. Each family is validated independently: the frame id is a bounded string; status is completed, failed or running; call_step_id equals the boundary (else missing_call_boundary); the alias is uniform across the boundary's frames (else persisted_import_alias_mismatch); the ordinal is a positive int with no leading junk; a nested marker gives unsupported_shape. Completed-only families are unlimited history and are never selected. Every non-completed member must belong to a single family, the current resumable family. Non-completed members in two families give ambiguous_resumable_call_frame, which is what the spec calls mixed bases. Within that family: more than one running member, or a duplicate ordinal, gives ambiguous_resumable_call_frame; a missing ordinal (a gap below the highest member, with completed members of the family counted as present) gives unsupported_shape. base_frame_id is that family's base, or None when every frame is completed. A non-Workflow-Lisp boundary has at most one non-completed frame across all families (else ambiguous_resumable_call_frame), and that frame is running_member. next_unused_retry_frame_id returns `<base>::retry::<lowest unused positive ordinal within the current family>`, counting completed members of that family, and is idempotent. The result never depends on mapping order. Remove the mapping-order helpers _retry_frame_id, _retry_family_base and _is_failed_retry_family_frame from calls.py once step 11 replaces their callers (validate_write_root_bindings then uses the lineage). Tests: new tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py, including a revisited call (completed visit::1 family with retries, running visit::2) that is accepted and selects visit::2; non-completed members in visit::1 and visit::2 rejected as ambiguous; next-ordinal computation scoped to the current family; and order independence under permuted frame_items.

7. The auditor (items 1, 2, 4, 7). Add orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (target under 400 lines). It imports nothing from workflow_lisp.migration_parity or procedure_identity_retirement, and no name or string in it contains receipt or audit/cache wording. It defines ResumeScopePath (frozen; call_frame_ids snapshotted to a tuple; root(), child(), projection_scope, as_context()), ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) with .error, and one _fail(reason, *, field, offending_value, candidate_count, call_boundary_step_id) builder that always emits all seven context keys. The message is always `Resume projection integrity audit failed: <reason>` and never includes a persisted value. Safe rendering, for untrusted values: offending_value is kept only for bool, int, or a str of at most 256 characters with no control characters. It is null for containers, oversized or control-bearing strings, and any other type, so contents are never echoed. Persisted mapping keys used in field paths (row names, frame ids) must be str within the same bound; otherwise the failure is unsupported_shape with field `steps` or `call_frames` and a null value. Keys are therefore validated before they are sorted or rendered: sorting is plain str order over already-validated keys, so mixed-type keys cannot raise before _fail. scope_path frame ids come only from frames that passed lineage validation, and are therefore bounded. It re-exports index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id, CallFrameRetryLineage, RetryFrameMember and CallFrameRetryLineageError from call_frame_lineage. audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path) takes the raw persisted state dict and runs in a fixed order, so the diagnostic is stable. (a) Container shapes and key safety: `steps` and `call_frames` must be mappings with safe keys, each frame a mapping. (b) Enumerate slots, mapping ResumeProjectionValidationError to unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress, with the field taken from the message. (c) Step rows in sorted name order: an absent step_id is skipped; otherwise check the type, then unknown, presentation mismatch, or unclaimed. (d) current_step: a missing step_id gives missing_required_identity; otherwise resolve it (out_of_scope or presentation mismatch). (e) Frames in sorted id order: a missing call_step_id gives missing_required_identity; a non-local id gives out_of_scope_step_id; a local non-boundary gives missing_call_boundary; more than one owner gives ambiguous_call_boundary; an alias that differs from boundary.import_alias gives persisted_import_alias_mismatch; an alias absent from bundle.imports gives missing_imported_bundle. (f) Group frames per boundary and run index_retry_lineage (visit-base partitioned, step 6), with frontend_kind from the imported bundle's provenance, translating lineage reasons. The auditor reads only its arguments: no loads, no checksum, no files, no mutation. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py builds bundles with WorkflowLoader in tmp_path, with one test per reason, plus scope path and expected_owner. Privacy cases: a malformed list id gives a null offending value; a 10k-character step_id gives a null offending value and a message without it; a 10k-character row name gives field `steps`; a non-string key in an in-memory steps or call_frames mapping gives unsupported_shape instead of TypeError; a secret placed in bound_inputs or context does not appear anywhere in the serialized diagnostic. Also a deepcopy non-mutation check, and one small source-scan test for the forbidden imports and words.

8. StateManager raw-document fidelity and envelopes (item 6). Two existing behaviours would break the stable diagnostic and the three-field delta. RunState.from_dict builds ForEachState(**entry), so a malformed for_each raises TypeError or AttributeError inside load() before any audit (orchestrator/state.py:160). And _write_state serialises RunState.to_dict(), which drops unknown root fields (orchestrator/state.py:335). Fixes: (a) RunState.from_dict converts a for_each entry to ForEachState only when it is a mapping that contains `items` and whose keys are a subset of the ForEachState fields; any other entry, or a non-mapping for_each container, is kept as its raw JSON value. to_dict already passes non-ForEachState entries through, and gains a pass-through for a non-mapping container. load() therefore never raises on loop bookkeeping, and the auditor sees the raw value and returns unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress. Runtime never consumes such entries, because the audit fails first. (b) load() also keeps the parsed JSON dict as self._persisted_document. (c) A private _record_terminal_error(error) re-reads state.json under the lock (falling back to _persisted_document only if the file is gone). It sets status='failed', error and updated_at on that raw dict and writes it atomically (temp file + rename), without going through to_dict. So current_step, the run tree, malformed bookkeeping and unknown root fields are byte-preserved, and fail_run is not called. It then mirrors status, error and updated_at into self.state, so a later ordinary write (session close) keeps the diagnostic. (d) record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason) validates reason against the four literals and builds the fixed message and context; record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error) persists the given diagnostic. Both delegate to (c). Tests: extend tests/test_state_manager.py. Compare state.json before and after each recorder, with an unknown root field and a malformed for_each entry present: only status, error and updated_at change. load() on a state with a malformed for_each entry (a list, an extra key, a non-mapping container) succeeds and round-trips the raw value. A later _write_state keeps the recorded error.

9. Root guard in the CLI (items 1 and 6). In orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, add the module-level `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, ResumeScopePath, audit_scope` and always call the bare name audit_scope. Move the _merge_observability_overrides persist block (currently ~lines 390-406, before the workflow load) to after the checksum precheck. On the non-force-restart path, right after validate_checksum passes, call audit_scope(workflow_bundle, state_manager.state.to_dict(), ResumeScopePath.root(state.workflow_file)). Because of step 8 this is the raw persisted bookkeeping, and a malformed for_each reaches the audit instead of failing in load(). On failure, call record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error), print the message (containing the reason) to stderr and return 1. This happens before the observability persist, open_executor_session, write_process_metadata, WorkflowExecutor construction and the prologue. Keep the existing checksum precheck unchanged (exit 1, nothing written). For .orc entries, the build artifacts written by _load_resume_workflow_bundle before this point are the documented exception (step 1 (iv)). Everything under the run root other than the three fields is unchanged. In the finally block, close the executor session as failed when the executor returned a projection or checksum error. A failing close is logged and cannot replace the persisted diagnostic (the error is already on disk and mirrored in memory). Tests: extend tests/test_resume_command.py. Substitute orchestrator.cli.commands.resume.audit_scope, open_executor_session and WorkflowExecutor with recorders to prove ordering. Check exit 1, stderr, and the three-field delta of state.json, including an unknown root field and a malformed for_each case (stable diagnostic, not a load traceback). Add an .orc resume with a stale step_id: the run root is unchanged except for the three fields, and build-directory writes are allowed.

10. Root guard in the executor (items 1 and 6). Add orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py with root_checksum_failure(state_manager, state) -> Optional[dict]. It recomputes the checksum through state_manager.calculate_checksum(Path(workflow_file)) and returns the reason: workflow_modified, missing_recorded_checksum, missing_workflow_path, or workflow_unavailable (FileNotFoundError). In orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, add a module-level import of audit_scope (called by the bare name) and a short _resume_root_guard(state), used in execute() before _execute_prologue only when resume is true and the state manager is not a CallFrameStateManager. On a checksum failure it calls record_workflow_checksum_mismatch and returns the recorded state without auditing. Otherwise it calls audit_scope(self.loaded_bundle, state, ResumeScopePath.root(...)); on failure it calls record_resume_projection_integrity_failure and returns the recorded state, with no prologue. The envelope is the delta of this write alone, as defined in step 1 (ii): the guard performs exactly one state write and opens or changes no session or process metadata. Session close stays the CLI's job (step 9). Tests (new tests/test_executor_resume_root_guard.py). (a) Executor-level: open a session on the state first, as the CLI does, snapshot state.json, run WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True) with executor.audit_scope substituted to fail; the delta is exactly status, error and updated_at, the open session record is still present, and the prologue was not entered. (b) A checksum race (workflow edited after the CLI audit, before execute): the checksum envelope with each reason literal, and no audit call. (c) CLI-level: with the second audit failing after the CLI audit passed, the persisted error equals the guard's diagnostic, runtime_observability shows the session closed as failed, process metadata is kept, and the only changes outside status, error and updated_at are that session-close record and the process metadata written before execute(). (d) A child call-frame executor never calls the root guard.

11. Reached-call validation and lineage selection (items 1 and 4). In orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, add the module-level audit_scope import and call the bare name. Replace the mapping-order branch of frame_id_with_overrides with lineage-based selection. Keep the order item 1 mandates. The parent's ordinary visit/start publication (executor.py:3070-3090; loops.py:933-1110) stays where it is, under the narrowed per-scope contract of step 1 (i): parent-scope identities were already audited before any mutation by the root guards, and nothing in this step writes to the callee frame or runs a callee effect before validation passes. In execute_call, keep the alias, bound-input, finalize, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input validation where they are. Before them, under resume_mode, call projection.resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, step_id) once (positional) on the parent slot index. Zero or several owners give a projection error. The boundary's import_alias selects the callee through workflow_import_bundle, so step['call'] and the persisted alias are only checked. The frame the call would occupy is its current visit frame id (`<prefix><step_id>::visit::<n>`, as frame_id_with_overrides derives it today). Before any lineage grouping, a completed frame with that id is rejected as resume_state_invalid_result(detail="completed_call_frame_id_collision"), whatever its call_step_id (matching, stale or missing). No child manager or executor is created and the frames are unchanged. A fresh retry id cannot collide, because next_unused_retry_frame_id counts completed members. Then run index_retry_lineage (visit-base partitioned) over this boundary's frames. With a running member: its validate_resume_checksum and validate_resume_bound_inputs run first and win on failure; then each failed predecessor, in ordinal order, gets validate_resume_checksum plus audit_scope(callee, pred['state'], scope.child(pred_id)); then audit_scope on the running member's state; then the child is built. With no running member, the predecessors are validated and audited, then the fresh frame is allocated. Derive the scope path by walking the _CallFrameStateManager.parent_manager chain, with a small helper in orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py. A ResumeProjectionIntegrityError or lineage error becomes {status: failed, exit_code: 2, error: exc.error}. When child_state fails with error.type resume_projection_integrity_error, or with the collision contract violation, return that error unchanged, not wrapped in call_failed. Tests: extend tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py with a stale caller, an alias change, two resumable frames, the retry lineage cases (failed predecessors audited, a gap, non-completed members across two visit bases), a revisited call with completed earlier-visit history that resumes, the exact collision context dict, precedence of call_resume_checksum_mismatch, and the callee frame untouched (substituting orchestrator.workflow.calls.audit_scope to observe ordering). Also a parent-delta test: after a reached-call audit failure, the parent's state differs from the pre-resume state only by the ordinary failed call-step snapshot, current_step, step_visits and (inside a loop) progress of the documented kind, and the selected callee frame is byte-identical.

12. Sticky non-routable failure and promotion (item 6). Add one predicate, is_sticky_resume_failure(error), in orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py. It is true for error.type resume_projection_integrity_error, and for the contract violation whose context.reason is call_resume_state_invalid and context.detail is completed_call_frame_id_collision. That detail is new in this change, so no existing routable failure becomes sticky. Use the predicate everywhere below. In WorkflowExecutor._handle_control_flow (orchestrator/workflow/executor.py ~line 3995), return '_stop' for it next to cycle_guard_exceeded, before goto, on_error=continue and strict_flow. Make sure the run-error promotion path (executor.py ~line 2043 and _execute_epilogue) copies that step error unchanged to the root error, and that later steps cannot clear or replace it. In orchestrator/workflow/loops.py (the for_each nested-failure break ~line 1067; the repeat_until condition and exhaustion path ~lines 1266-1420), stop at once: the loop step fails with the same error, with no next iteration, no condition evaluation and no exhaustion result. In orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, record_step_result and record_settled_result keep finalization running for configured cleanup. When the run already carries a sticky diagnostic, a cleanup failure is recorded as status failed with failure={step, step_id, error: the cleanup's projection error or null}, and state['error'] is never replaced. A projection error raised only inside finalization becomes the run error and failure.error. Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py drives YAML workflows through the resume command or the executor, using a stale nested call identity to trigger the error. It covers success, failure and always gotos, on_error=continue, for_each and repeat_until, and a finally block. It also checks that a completed-frame collision is promoted unchanged to the root error with its exact context and is not consumed by on_error=continue or a failure goto.

13. Forensic current_step in observability (item 6). In orchestrator/observability/report.py, add _is_forensic_current_step(state): true when status is failed and error.type is resume_projection_integrity_error or workflow_checksum_mismatch. In build_status_snapshot (~lines 299-332), treat that step as not current: status and summary pending, current_visit_count null, counted as pending. render_status_markdown then never shows 'in progress'. Make the heartbeat helper (~line 234) ignore the step. Check orchestrator/dashboard/cursor.py and orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py. The classifier already returns FAILED before any heartbeat check, so change the cursor only if it reports the node as live. Tests: extend tests/test_observability_report.py.

14. Verification, documentation routes and wrap-up. Run pytest --collect-only on every new or renamed test module. Run the narrow selectors from steps 2-13, then the neighbouring suites: tests/test_resume_command.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py, tests/test_state_manager.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py, tests/test_observability_report.py, tests/test_at68_resume_force_restart.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py and the workflow_lisp build tests. End-to-end smoke check: `python -m orchestrator run` then `resume` on workflows/examples/for_each_demo.yaml and finally_demo.yaml; hand-edit one state.json step_id and confirm the exit-1 projection diagnostic and the three-field delta. Also hand-add an unknown root field and confirm it survives. When the implementation lands, update the maintained documentation routes so readers are not sent to stale status. docs/capability_status_matrix.md (the procedure-first reuse row, ~line 34): replace the statement that the 2026-07-13 design-and-planning plan is the live selector and that runtime hardening is not implemented with the implemented status, pointing to the specs/state.md section, the acceptance entries and the new test modules, and keeping the migration-wave gate wording accurate. docs/design/README.md 'Runtime And Observability Direction' (~line 79): route to the specs/state.md section and mark the 2026-07-13 plan as historical. docs/index.md: fix its reference to the 2026-07-13 plan the same way. Run consistency checks on those three files (grep for the 2026-07-13 plan name and 'does not implement runtime hardening'). Check that new modules stay under 500 lines. Commit after each green step (no --no-verify). Open assumptions to confirm with the user: (a) the CLI audit also runs for status 'completed' runs, because under the literal ordering it precedes the early 'already completed' return; (b) finalization.failure.error is null for ordinary cleanup failures only when the run carries a sticky diagnostic, and non-projection behaviour is otherwise unchanged; (c) the reached-call mutation boundary is narrowed as in step 1 (i), which item 1's ordering requires; (d) the .orc build-artifact exception of step 1 (iv); (e) over-long or control-bearing scalars are rendered as null, beyond item 7's container rule; (f) the completed-frame collision keeps its mandated contract_violation shape but is sticky and promoted unchanged; (g) ordinary writes after a failure envelope (session close) still use to_dict, so unknown root fields are guaranteed only across the failure writes; a general fix is an unrelated refactor.

value.account:
Changed (all committed): spec section in specs/state.md, acceptance entries 201-216 and plan doc docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity.md; typed frontend_kind provenance for Workflow Lisp bundles; loader duplicate-import-alias check (orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py); projection data (call-boundary import_alias, repeat_until max_iterations); resume_slots.py (slot enumeration, loop bookkeeping validation); call_frame_lineage.py (retry lineage by visit base); resume_projection_integrity.py (audit_scope, diagnostics, is_sticky_resume_failure); StateManager raw-document fidelity and the two failure recorders; CLI root guard in resume.py; executor root guard (resume_root_guard.py); reached-call validation and lineage-based frame selection in calls.py; sticky non-routable failure in executor/loops/finalization; forensic current_step in observability and dashboard cursor; doc routing in docs/index.md, capability_status_matrix.md, design/README.md. The work was split across subagents and each step has its own tests. 644 tests passed in the neighbouring suites I re-ran at the end (resume command, subworkflow calls, projection, state manager, loader, observability, force-restart, lexical default resume, build artifacts and every new module). A manual smoke run (for_each_demo run, then resume, then hand-edited stale step_id and an unknown root field) gave the unknown_explicit_step_id diagnostic; only error and updated_at changed (status was already failed from my edit) and the unknown root field survived.

Decisions and deviations: (1) The persisted-key bound is 4096, not 256, because generated stdlib step ids reach ~550 chars and frame ids ~850; scalar offending_value stays at 256. (2) Item 3 (successful exhaustion needs a completed loop row) contradicts existing lexical-checkpoint-restore tests that delete the loop row; the spec wins, so the audit fails closed with invalid_loop_progress and I rewrote those tests (6 in the restore module, 3 in test_resume_command.py) to assert the fail-closed diagnostic. That makes loop-frame restore from a row-less terminal state unreachable; recorded in the plan doc. (3) The import-alias check uses SafeLoader rather than PreservingLoader to avoid a circular import; message format 'imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias (line L, column C; ...)' is my layout around the fixed pieces. (4) Reached-call diagnostics use the auditor's private builder (_Audit.fail); a public builder would be cleaner. (5) Lineage selection lives in execute_call rather than frame_id_with_overrides because the collision check needs the plain visit id first. (6) Added some loop-validation messages not in the brief (current_index out of range, completed_* must be a list). (7) A projection error arising only inside finalization cannot be produced from YAML (loader rejects call in finally), so that case is tested at the FinalizationController level. (8) Several old tests were changed because the earlier, correct root audit now rejects before they reached their old assertions (four tests in test_subworkflow_calls.py removed/replaced, two updated).

Not covered / caveats: the in-loop parent-delta test for reached-call failure was not written; the finally_demo smoke run was not repeated by me (for_each_demo only); the .orc stale-step_id resume test exists but I did not separately re-verify build-dir behaviour beyond it passing. A full-suite run by the step-12 agent showed 77 failures versus 82 on a HEAD copy, none new; they are pre-existing failures in workflow_lisp post_wcc/phase_stdlib/semantic_ir/key_migrations and environment-dependent tests, and I did not fix them. Some new modules' sibling files (state.py ~990 lines, report.py ~630) were already over 500 lines. Co-author trailer is Claude Sonnet 5.5 per the brief; one agent used Opus 5.5 for two commits. Considered and rejected: reading a read-only .orc compile route (out of scope), exempting restore-recoverable loop state from the audit (not in the spec).
